newsitem.title: FRANCE: France to try again for Cr Foncier ally.
newsitem.headline: France to try again for Cr Foncier ally.

text.p: The French finance ministry said on Thursday it wanted a new search launched for a shareholder partner for the troubled home loans group Credit Foncier de France.

The ministry said in a statement it had taken note of the discussions on Credit Foncier which had taken place in the past few weeks and led by state-appointed mediator Philippe Rouvillois and reiterated that the group could not carry on without access to financial markets and a credible partner.
"The government has always seen this partnership as a priority," said the statement. "That is why it wants a new period opened to look for a core shareholder for the group."
"The State will consider all proposals formulated and pay particular attention to their industrial, social and financial credibility," it said.

Rouvillois had been called in by Prime Minister alain Juppe to mediate after a campaign of staff, union and some political resistance to a finance ministry plan involving a break-up in which part of Foncier would be taken over by cooperatively run Credit Immobilier and the rest wound down.

Credit Foncier announced 1995 losses of 10.8 billion francs in April 1996 had failed to find a rescue partner by an end-July deadline set by the ministry and has been operating by special exception despite not meeting standard solvency levels.
The finance ministry announced the break-up plan last year after the failure to find a partner but Credit Immobilier has backed off as mediation and the campaign against the plan drag on.

The group expects to report a profit of around a billion francs for last year and staff have been pushing for other solutions than the ministry's plan on the grounds that the group could continue to operate with the help of a partner and fresh capital.
The ministry statement on Thursday did not give timing details for the new partner search but said restructuring would have to continue in the meantime.
